LESSON: INVERTEBRATES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 1.2: Invertebrates

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Invertebrates. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the common features of invertebrates?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify common invertebrates in the environment
2. practise precautions in handling invertebrates
3. describe the general characteristics of invertebrates
4. appreciate the importance of invertebrates in nature
5. identify main parts of the human circulatory system
6. describe functions of main parts of the human circulatory system

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INVERTEBRATES
Subject: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Invertebrates helps you succeed in SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: INVERTEBRATES
Study Invertebrates like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify common invertebrates in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to identify common invertebrates in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify common invertebrates in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Invertebrates” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify common invertebrates in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

What this means
In this part you learn to practise precautions in handling invertebrates. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

Your turn

PART 5: Identify main parts of the human circulatory system

What this means

2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe functions of main parts of the human circulatory system. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Invertebrates is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Invertebrates” around your school. (skill: identify common invertebrates in the environment)

Example 2: Say why Invertebrates matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: practise precautions in handling invertebrates)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Invertebrates this week. (skill: describe the general characteristics of invertebrates)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Invertebrates” around your school. (skill: appreciate the importance of invertebrates in nature)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Invertebrates to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify common invertebrates in the environment.
3. Practise this skill: practise precautions in handling invertebrates.
4. Practise this skill: describe the general characteristics of invertebrates.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Invertebrates from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Invertebrates: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Invertebrates?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the common features of invertebrates?
2. What is the human circulatory system made up of?
3. What measures enhance a healthy human circulatory system?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Invertebrates means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify common invertebrates in the environment.
5. Be able to: practise precautions in handling invertebrates.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
